communicates.content: Watson, when you reach London you would oblige me by driving at once to Baker Street with our friend here, and remaining with him until I see you again.

events.label: Holmes allocates the spare bedroom to Percy Phelps and schedules his arrival for breakfast

communicates.speaker: character_sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: Mr. Phelps can have the spare bedroom to-night, and I will be with you in time for breakfast, for there is a train which will take me into Waterloo at eight.

events.label: Holmes tells them their London investigation will be done tomorrow

communicates.speaker: character_sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: We can do that to-morrow. I think that just at present I can be of more immediate use here.

events.label: Phelps says he hopes Holmes will be back tomorrow night and Holmes responds he hardly expects to return to Briarbrae

communicates.speaker: character_percy_phelps
communicates.content: You might tell them at Briarbrae that I hope to be back to-morrow night,

events.label: Holmes answers that he hardly expects to go back to Briarbrae

communicates.speaker: character_sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: I hardly expect to go back to Briarbrae,

events.label: Holmes tells Watson to go to bed and be fresh for whatever may await tomorrow

communicates.speaker: character_sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: Now, my dear fellow, we can't help matters by making ourselves nervous about them, so let me implore you to go to bed and so be fresh for whatever may await us to-morrow.

events.label: Holmes enters Phelps's room the next morning and says he has only a scratch from his own clumsiness

communicates.speaker: character_sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: "Tut, it is only a scratch through my own clumsiness,"

events.label: Holmes says breakfast will be after breakfast and that there was no answer from his cabman advertisement

communicates.speaker: character_sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: After breakfast, my dear Watson. Remember that I have breathed thirty miles of Surrey air this morning. I suppose that there has been no answer from my cabman advertisement? Well, well, we cannot expect to score every time.

events.label: Holmes answers Phelps during breakfast and introduces a dramatic reveal

communicates.speaker: character_sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: Well, then, said Holmes, with a mischievous twinkle, "I suppose that you have no objection to helping me?"

events.label: Phelps screams while lifting the cover revealing a cylinder of blue-grey paper in the dish

communicates.speaker: character_percy_phelps
communicates.content: a scream

events.label: Phelps kisses Holmes's hand and says he saved his honor

communicates.speaker: character_percy_phelps
communicates.content: God bless you! You have saved my honour.

events.label: Holmes says his own was at stake and that it is hateful to fail in a case

communicates.speaker: character_sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: Well, my own was at stake, you know... I assure you it is just as hateful to me to fail in a case as it can be to you to blunder over a commission.

events.label: Holmes places the explanation and describes obtaining the cylinder from behind a board after Joseph Harrison enters the room

communicates.speaker: character_sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: I'll tell you what I did first, and how I came to do it afterwards

events.label: Holmes says Joseph Harrison executed an intrusion at the bedroom and retrieved the cylinder from a hiding place
Joseph Harrison takes a knife and gets into the room by opening the window and lifting the bar
Holmes says he grasped Joseph Harrison twice after Joseph flew at him with the knife and Holmes got a cut over his knuckles
Holmes says he wired full particulars to Forbes

communicates.speaker: character_sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: wired full particulars

events.label: Holmes explains Joseph Harrison's character and that he would do anything to improve fortunes

communicates.speaker: character_sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: I am afraid Joseph's character is a rather deeper and more dangerous one... From what I have heard from him this morning, I gather that he has lost heavily in dabbling with stocks, and that he is ready to do anything on earth to better his fortunes. Being an absolutely selfish man, when a chance presented itself he did not allow either his sister's happiness or your reputation to hold his hand.

events.label: Joseph Harrison enters an office through the Charles Street door and walks into a room immediately after someone leaves
Joseph Harrison finds no one present and rings a bell
Joseph Harrison notices a paper on a table at the moment he rings the bell
Joseph Harrison thrusts a State document into his pocket and leaves
A commissionnaire takes time to notice the bell and draws attention to it after a few minutes
Joseph Harrison goes to Woking by the first train, examines the document, and conceals it for later removal
Holmes returns suddenly to the room
Joseph Harrison is bundled out of his room without warning
At least two of the group remain in the room to prevent Joseph Harrison from regaining the treasure
Joseph Harrison attempts to steal in but is prevented by wakefulness
Watson says he does not remember taking the usual draught that night

communicates.speaker: character_watson
communicates.content: I remember.

events.label: Holmes explains that Joseph Harrison took steps to make the draught efficacious and relied on Watson being unconscious

communicates.speaker: character_sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: I fancy that he had taken steps to make that draught efficacious, and that he quite relied upon your being unconscious.

events.label: Holmes states he understood Joseph Harrison would repeat the attempt whenever it could be done with safety

communicates.speaker: character_sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: Of course, I understood that he would repeat the attempt whenever it could be done with safety.

events.label: Watson leaving the room gives Joseph Harrison the chance he wanted
Holmes keeps Miss Harrison in the room all day
Holmes gives Joseph Harrison the idea that the coast is clear, then keeps guard as described
Holmes permits Joseph Harrison to take the papers from the hiding-place
Watson asks whether there is another point Holmes can make clear

communicates.speaker: character_watson
communicates.content: Is there any other point which I can make clear?

events.label: Watson asks why Joseph Harrison tried the window on the first occasion rather than the door

communicates.speaker: character_watson
communicates.content: Why did he try the window on the first occasion, when he might have entered by the door?

events.label: Holmes states that reaching the door would require passing seven bedrooms

communicates.speaker: character_sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: In reaching the door he would have to pass seven bedrooms.

events.label: Holmes states that Joseph Harrison could get out onto the lawn with ease

communicates.speaker: character_sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: On the other hand, he could get out on to the lawn with ease.

events.label: Phelps asks whether Joseph Harrison had any murderous intention and states the knife was only a tool

communicates.speaker: character_percy_phelps
communicates.content: The knife was only meant as a tool.

events.label: Holmes responds that he can only say for certain that Joseph Harrison is a gentleman whose mercy he would be unwilling to trust

communicates.speaker: character_sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: I can only say for certain that Mr. Joseph Harrison is a gentleman to whose mercy I should be extremely unwilling to trust.

clues.significance: Percy Phelps discovered that the copy remained in place while the original secret treaty was missing from the desk after the theft.
Holmes reported that the cylinder of blue-grey paper was retrieved by Joseph Harrison from behind a square board covering a T joint behind the carpet in Phelps's bedroom.
Holmes treated the State document as valuable evidence when explaining that Joseph Harrison pocketed a State document after his eyes caught the paper on the table.
